summary:
Configured redundant L3 connectivity between node1's private network (node3) and node2's private network (node4) carried over both independent node1-node2 links, with automatic failover and full node-restart persistence verified on all four nodes.

Topology discovery: node1 eth1/eth2 and node2 eth1/eth2 are the two independent uplinks between node1-node2; node1 eth3 connects to node3's enp8s0, node2 eth3 connects to node4's enp8s0 (confirmed via targeted ping tests, since interfaces carried no IPs initially).

Implementation:
- node1: bond0 (Linux bonding, mode balance-rr, miimon 100) over eth1+eth2, IP 172.20.0.1/30 to node2; eth3 = 192.168.1.1/24 (node3's subnet). IP forwarding enabled globally and per-interface. Static route to 192.168.2.0/24 via bond0.
- node2: mirrored — bond0 172.20.0.2/30, eth3 = 192.168.2.1/24 (node4's subnet), route to 192.168.1.0/24 via bond0.
- node3/node4: enp8s0 statically addressed (192.168.1.2/24, 192.168.2.2/24) via existing NetworkManager profiles with a static route to the other private subnet via its local node1/node2 gateway — persists natively through NetworkManager.
- Persistence on node1/node2: a systemd oneshot unit (antrieb-links.service, enabled, WantedBy=multi-user.target) reapplies the bonding/IP/forwarding/route configuration at boot, since SONiC's interfaces-config.service only manages eth0/lo and does not touch eth1-3.
- Discovered and worked around a virtio/bonding limitation: 802.3ad (LACP) mode failed because virtio-net can't report link speed/duplex (dmesg: "failed to get link speed/duplex"), so switched to balance-rr, which works cleanly and actively load-balances across both links (confirmed via matched tx_packet counters growing symmetrically on eth1/eth2 for a test ping burst).
- Also discovered that the platform's virtual point-to-point links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer's carrier state (verified: bringing node1's eth1 down did not clear LOWER_UP on node2's eth1), so failover was correctly demonstrated as a full link outage (both endpoints down), which is the realistic failure model — 0% packet loss for node3↔node4 traffic in that state, and clean automatic recovery once both ends were restored.
- Ran the mandatory node-restart protocol on all four nodes sequentially (one at a time, quorum/service preserved): captured pre-restart boot_id, restarted via `reboot`/`systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed a new boot_id, and verified bonding/routes/forwarding/NetworkManager config and node3↔node4 connectivity recovered on each.
actions_performed: Mapped node1/node2/node3/node4 interface topology via targeted temporary-IP ping tests since interfaces carried no addresses
Diagnosed and resolved a virtio-net + LACP (802.3ad) incompatibility, switching to balance-rr bonding
Configured bond0 (balance-rr, miimon 100) on node1 and node2 spanning both independent uplinks
Configured node1 eth3 (192.168.1.1/24) and node2 eth3 (192.168.2.1/24) as private-network gateways for node3/node4
Enabled global and per-interface IPv4 forwarding on node1 and node2
Added static routes on node1, node2, node3, node4 to reach the opposite private subnet
Persisted node3/node4 static addressing and routes via existing NetworkManager 'Wired connection 2' profiles
Created and enabled a systemd oneshot unit (antrieb-links.service) on node1 and node2 to reapply bonding/IP/forwarding/route config at boot
Verified active-active use of both links via symmetric tx_packet counters on eth1/eth2 during a ping burst
Disrupted link A (eth1) at both node1 and node2 to simulate a full link outage, confirmed 0% packet loss for node3<->node4 traffic, then restored and confirmed recovery and renewed dual-link usage

Executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1, node2, node3, and node4 sequentially: captured baseline boot_id, restarted, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified recovered bonding/network/connectivity state

evidence.requirement: Traffic between node3 and node4 private networks carried over both node1-node2 links (active-active)
evidence.summary: bond0 (balance-rr) established on node1/node2 over eth1+eth2; node3->node4 ping succeeds; tx_packets on eth1 and eth2 both incremented by 23 during a 40-packet burst, proving both links carry traffic

evidence.requirement: node3/node4 keep reaching each other when either link is taken out of service
evidence.summary: Baseline 0% loss; link A (eth1) disabled at both endpoints (realistic full-link-outage model, since platform links don't propagate one-sided down); node3->node4 ping showed 0% loss over remaining link B; link A restored, bond returned to MII up on both slaves, and both links resumed carrying traffic evenly

Baseline boot_id 34192023...; reboot acknowledged and connection reset observed; post-restart boot_id 2b968bb7... (changed); antrieb-links.service active, bonding/routes/forwarding restored, node3->node4 ping 0% loss

Baseline boot_id 8e8823ec...; reboot acknowledged, connection reset/timeout observed during restart; post-restart boot_id 0caec094... (changed); bonding/routes/forwarding restored, node4->node3 ping 0% loss (after transient neighbor-cache loss settled)

Baseline boot_id 83a0a80f...; systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection timeout/reset observed; post-restart boot_id a6e47589... (changed); NetworkManager-managed enp8s0 static IP/route intact, ping to node4 0% loss
Baseline boot_id 0581c914...; systemctl reboot acknowledged, connection timeout/reset observed; post-restart boot_id 547e58a1... (changed); enp8s0 static IP/route intact, ping to node3 0% loss

evidence.requirement: Final cross-cluster health confirmation after all restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart-cycle check on node1 and node2 shows both bond0 slaves MII up and all required routes present on both nodes
